claim: Hematopoietic stem cells emerge in the embryo from an aortic-derived tissue called the hemogenic endothelium (HE).
source: Hematopoietic stem cells emerge in the embryo from an aortic-derived tissue called the hemogenic endothelium (HE).
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the origin of hematopoietic stem cells.

claim: Two cell types emerge from the aortic floor with radically different morphodynamics in the zebrafish embryo.
source: Here we show, in the zebrafish embryo, that two cell types emerge from the aortic floor with radically different morphodynamics.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by live imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The first type of EHT cell emergence is characterized by reinforcement of apicobasal polarity and maintenance of the apical/luminal membrane until release.
source: While the first type is characterized by reinforcement of apicobasal polarity and maintenance of the apical/luminal membrane until release, the second type emerges via a dynamic process reminiscent of trans-endothelial migration.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by live imaging data and analysis of polarity markers.

claim: The second type of EHT cell emerges via a dynamic process reminiscent of trans-endothelial migration.
source: While the first type is characterized by reinforcement of apicobasal polarity and maintenance of the apical/luminal membrane until release, the second type emerges via a dynamic process reminiscent of trans-endothelial migration.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by live imaging observations.

claim: The balance between the two emergence types depends on tuning apicobasal polarity at the level of the HE.
source: Interfering with Runx1 function suggests that the balance between the two emergence types depends on tuning apicobasal polarity at the level of the HE.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from Runx1 interference experiments.

claim: Pard3ba is sensitive to interference with Runx1 activity in aortic endothelial cells.
source: In support of this and unexpectedly, we show that Pard3ba – one of the four Pard3 proteins expressed in the zebrafish – is sensitive to interference with Runx1 activity, in aortic endothelial cells.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR and RNAscope data showing changes in Pard3ba expression upon Runx1 interference.

claim: There is a signaling cross talk controlling cell polarity and its associated features between aortic and hemogenic cells.
source: This supports the idea of a signaling cross talk controlling cell polarity and its associated features, between aortic and hemogenic cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Pard3ba expression in aortic cells is sensitive to Runx1 activity.

claim: ArhGEF11/PDZ-RhoGEF plays an essential role in controlling the HE-endothelial cell dynamic interface.
source: In addition, using new transgenic fish lines that express Junctional Adhesion Molecules and functional interference, we bring evidence for the essential role of ArhGEF11/PDZ-RhoGEF in controlling the HE-endothelial cell dynamic interface, including cell-cell intercalation, which is ultimately required for emergence completion.
evidence: This is supported by morpholino and CRISPR experiments showing impaired EHT progression.

claim: Cell-cell intercalation is required for EHT emergence completion.
source: In addition, using new transgenic fish lines that express Junctional Adhesion Molecules and functional interference, we bring evidence for the essential role of ArhGEF11/PDZ-RhoGEF in controlling the HE-endothelial cell dynamic interface, including cell-cell intercalation, which is ultimately required for emergence completion.
evidence: This is supported by observations of impaired intercalation in ArhGEF11 interference experiments.

claim: HSCs with full regenerative potential are generated during a narrow time window of few days during embryonic development.
source: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) endowed with full regenerative potential in adult vertebrates are generated during a narrow-time window of few days during embryonic development.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of developmental hematopoiesis.

claim: HSCs emerge from intra-embryonic aortic vessels.
source: These cells, at the root of all blood and immune cells in the body, emerge from intra-embryonic aortic vessels and, more specifically, from a specialized type of vascular tissue called the hemogenic endothelium (HE, Wu and Hirschi, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The autonomous production of repopulating HSCs occurs within the Aorta-Gonad-Mesonephros (AGM) region before their appearance in other hematopoietic organs.
source: A series of seminal studies have evidenced the autonomous production of repopulating HSCs within an intraembryonic region called the Aorta-Gonad-Mesonephros (AGM), before their appearance in other hematopoietic organs (Medvinsky et al., 1993; Müller et al., 1994; Garcia-Porrero et al., 1995; Medvinsky and Dzierzak, 1996; Cumano et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to seminal studies.

claim: The endothelial origin of HSCs has been evidenced.
source: Thereafter, the endothelial origin of HSCs was evidenced (Jaffredo et al., 1998; de Bruijn et al., 2002; North et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to key studies.

claim: The direct visualization of the emergence of precursors of HSPCs from the dorsal aorta was achieved in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo.
source: The direct visualization, in real-time, of the emergence of precursors of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) from the dorsal aorta, termed the Endothelial-to-Hematopoietic Transition (EHT), was finally achieved in vitro (Eilken et al., 2009), ex vivo from mouse sections (Boisset et al., 2010), and in vivo in the zebrafish embryo (Bertrand et al., 2010; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010), using live microscopy.
evidence: This is supported by citations to key studies that visualized the EHT process.

claim: The HE is characterized by inherent heterogeneity.
source: The HE is characterized by inherent heterogeneity and is not only contributing to the formation of precursors to long-term HSCs (pre-HSCs) but also to more restricted progenitors (Hadland and Yoshimoto, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: The HE contributes to the formation of both pre-HSCs and more restricted progenitors.
source: The HE is characterized by inherent heterogeneity and is not only contributing to the formation of precursors to long-term HSCs (pre-HSCs) but also to more restricted progenitors (Hadland and Yoshimoto, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation and represents established knowledge.

claim: EGFP-podxl2 is enriched at the luminal side of crescent-shaped EHT undergoing cells.
source: We observed that eGFP-podxl2 is enriched at the luminal side of crescent-shaped EHT undergoing cells (see Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 1—video 1 (z-stack at t=0) and their legends for the details of the luminal/apical membrane evolution through time).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: EHT pol+ cells are characterized by enrichment of eGFP-podxl2 at the luminal membrane.
source: We observed that eGFP-podxl2 is enriched at the luminal side of crescent-shaped EHT undergoing cells (see Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 1—video 1 (z-stack at t=0) and their legends for the details of the luminal/apical membrane evolution through time). Thereafter, these cells will be referred to as EHT pol+ cells.
evidence: This is a definition based on observed data.

claim: EHT pol- cells do not show enrichment of eGFP-podxl2 at the luminal membrane.
source: Importantly, these cells do not show any enrichment of eGFP-podxl2 at the luminal membrane and will be referred to as EHT pol- cells.
evidence: This is a definition based on observed data from imaging.

claim: The ratio between EHT pol+ and EHT pol- cells is approximately 2/1.
source: Finally, we have estimated that the ratio between EHT pol+and EHT pol- cells is of approximately 2/1, irrespective of the imaging time window and of the localization of emergence along the aortic antero-posterior axis (starting from the most anterior part of the AGM (at the limit between the balled and the elongated yolk) down to the caudal part of the aorta facing the CHT).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of imaging data.

claim: Both EHT pol+ and EHT pol- cells divide during emergence and maintain their respective morphological characteristics after completing abscission.
source: We observed that both EHT pol+and EHT pol- cells divide during the emergence and remain with their respective morphological characteristics after completing abscission (Figure 1—figure supplement 2); hence they appear as pairs of cells that exit the aortic wall sequentially (as shown Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This is supported by time-lapse imaging data.

claim: Both EHT pol+ and EHT pol- cells express reporters driven by the hematopoietic marker CD41.
source: We also observed that both EHT pol+and EHT pol- cells express reporters driven by the hematopoietic marker CD41 (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), which indicates that they are both endowed with hematopoietic potential.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data showing CD41 expression.

claim: HE cells do not appear to be polarized at the initiation of the EHT time-window based on the absence of Podxl2 enrichment at luminal membranes.
source: Surprisingly, confocal microscopy using our eGFP-podxl2 and mKate2-podxl2 expressing fish lines revealed that HE cells do not appear to be polarized, based on the absence of Podxl2 enrichment at luminal membranes, at the initiation of the EHT time-window and later (at approximately 28–30 hpf, Figure 2—figure supplement 1 see also at 35 hpf Figure 2A, top left panel, green arrows and Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and at 48–55 hpf Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data.

claim: The cytoplasm of HE cells is filled with membrane vesicles that carry eGFP-podxl2.
source: Interestingly, the cytoplasm of characteristic elongated HE cells located on the aortic floor is filled with more-or-less large membrane vesicles that carry eGFP-podxl2 (the largest vesicles reaching approximately 30 µm in diameter).
evidence: This is based on confocal microscopy observations.

claim: Loss of apicobasal polarity features of HE cells at 28-30 hpf may be part of the programme that initiates the EHT process.
source: Consequently, loss of apicobasal polarity features of HE cells at 28–30 hpf may be part of the programme that initiates the EHT process.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of non-polarized HE cells.

claim: Expression of dt-runx1 leads to accumulation of HE cells in comparison to controls.
source: Firstly, using 48–55 hpf Tg(dt-runx1) embryos and live imaging we observed, in comparison to controls, a significant accumulation of HE cells (see Figure 3A, top and bottom panels (HE, arrowheads), see also the quantifications Figure 3B, top graph, median value of 17 cells for controls and 25 cells for mutants).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of live imaging data.

claim: Expression of dt-runx1 leads to an increase in the proportion of EHT pol+ cells.
source: We also observed the unusual tendency for the accumulation of EHT pol+ cells (Figure 3A, green and pink arrows), with a maximum value of 3 cells per embryo for controls that reached the unusual - never observed in control conditions -, values of 11, 9, and 8 cells for 3 mutants out of 7 (Figure 3B, middle graph).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of imaging data.

claim: Expression of dt-runx1 does not significantly modify the number of EHT pol- cells.
source: Finally, we did not observe any significant modification in the number of EHT pol- cells (same median values for both controls and mutants, the values oscillating between 0 and 1 cell per embryo, with only one example of an embryo exhibiting two apparent EHT pol- cells [Figure 3B, bottom graph]).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of imaging data.

claim: Cells that accumulate in the aortic floor of dt-Runx1 mutants are of hematopoietic nature.
source: Secondly, using 48–55 hpf Tg(dt-runx1) embryos and controls Tg(Kdrl:eGFP) we confirm, by whole mount in situ hybridization performed with an RNAscope probe specific for myb (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), that the cells that accumulate in the aortic floor of dt-Runx1 mutants are indeed of hematopoietic nature (see the cells with RNAscope spots in magenta or marked by blue arrows, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, zoomed areas).
evidence: This is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data.

claim: There is a specific increase of hemogenic/EHT cells in aortic floors of dt-Runx1 mutants in comparison to controls.
source: However, cell counts after segmentation using the Imaris software confirmed, based on cell localization, the specific increase of hemogenic/EHT cells in aortic floors of mutants median values of 34 and 16.5 for mutants and controls, respectively, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B (right panel) while no difference was measured for endothelial roof cells between mutants and controls (left panel).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of RNAscope data.

claim: The increase of pre-hematopoietic cells in the aortic floor in dt-Runx1 mutants correlates with a decrease in hematopoietic cells lodging in the sub-aortic region.
source: Importantly, the increase of pre-hematopoietic cells in the aortic floor in the mutants correlates with a decrease in hematopoietic cells lodging in the sub-aortic region, reinforcing the idea of impairment in EHT cell emergence (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, right panel).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of cell counts in different regions.

claim: There is an important increase in myb expression by hemogenic cells in the floor of dt-Runx1 mutants in comparison to controls.
source: Finally, quantification of the number of myb RNAscope spots per segmented hemogenic cells highlights the important increase in expression by hemogenic cells in the floor of dt-Runx1 mutants, in comparison to controls (with median values of 4 and 0, respectively) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of RNAscope data.

claim: Embryos obtained from outcrossing Tg(dt-runx1) and Tg(Kdrl:mKate2-podxl2) fishes contain polarized HE cells based on enrichment of the polarity marker at luminal membranes.
source: Thirdly, between 30 and 55 hpf, using live confocal microscopy and contrarily to what we observed with our fish lines expressing either eGFP-podxl2 (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2) or mKate2-podxl2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A) in which HE cells appear to be non-polarized, embryos obtained from outcrossing Tg(dt-runx1) and Tg(Kdrl:mKate2-podxl2) fishes appear to contain polarized HE cells, based on enrichment of the polarity marker at luminal membranes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is based on confocal microscopy observations.

claim: Hematopoiesis is affected at 5 dpf in dt-Runx1 mutants as shown by a significant increase in the number of hematopoietic cells in the thymus.
source: Fifthly, hematopoiesis is affected far downstream of emergence, as attested by the significant increase, at 5 dpf, in the number of hematopoietic cells in the thymus of dt-Runx1 mutants, in comparison to control siblings (see Figure 3—figure supplement 3A for images after cell segmentation with the Imaris software accompanied by Figure 3—video 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 3B for quantifications showing significant increase in thymus volume [left panel] owed to the increase in cell number [middle panel] rather than in cell volume [right panel]).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of thymus morphometry.

claim: Pard3ba mRNAs are expressed in the aorta during the EHT time-window.
source: Among the four Pard3 proteins expressed in the zebrafish (encoded by four different genes and non-including splicing variants), we describe the specific expression of Pard3ba, in the aorta, during the EHT time-window.
evidence: This is supported by RNAscope in situ hybridization data.

claim: The expression of Pard3ba is sensitive to interference with the transcription factor Runx1.
source: We show that the expression of Pard3ba is sensitive to interference with the transcription factor Runx1 whose function is essential for EHT completion (Kissa and Herbomel, 2010) and for regulating HSC number (Adamo et al., 2009; North et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR and RNAscope data comparing control and dt-Runx1 conditions.

claim: Pard3ba mRNAs are localized heterogeneously along the aortic axis with enrichment in specific regions (MERs).
source: To visualize more precisely expression levels in the vascular system in the trunk (more specifically in the aorta and the underlying vein), we zoomed in this region (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D) and observed a homogeneous localization of Pard3aa and Pard3ab mRNAs as well as, strikingly in the case of Pard3ba, a quite heterogeneous localization of mRNAs unequally concentrated along the aortic axis (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D middle panel and see also Figure 4C, top panel; these will be referred thereon as Pard3ba mRNA enriched regions (MERs)).
evidence: This is based on RNAscope in situ hybridization data.

claim: Expression of dt-Runx1 leads to an increase of approximately 300% in Pard3ba spots per aortic segment.
source: Quantification of RNAscope spots per aortic segment and per hemogenic/EHT cell using Imaris revealed an increase of almost 300% for the former when comparing controls and mutants (median values of 65.00 and 167.50 for controls and dt-Runx1 mutants, respectively, Figure 4D) and that virtually no Pard3ba mRNA was detected in the latter (median values of 0.00 spots per hemogenic/EHT cell for both controls and dt-Runx1 mutants, Figure 4E).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of RNAscope data.

claim: Pard3ba mRNAs are preferentially localized in the direct vicinity of hemogenic/EHT cells.
source: Finally and importantly, in wild-type embryos, the Pard3ba mRNAs are preferentially localized in the direct vicinity of hemogenic/EHT cells (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: This is based on spatial analysis of RNAscope data.

claim: More than 50% of Pard3ba spots are localized within 5-10 µm of hemogenic/EHT cells.
source: Indeed, more than 50% of Pard3ba spots are localized within 5–10 µm of hemogenic/EHT cells (Figure 4G, middle panel), and more than 75% of spots are localized within a 5–20 µm distance (Figure 4G right panel).
evidence: This is based on quantitative spatial analysis of RNAscope data.

claim: The number of hemogenic/EHT cells strongly correlates with the spatial densification of Pard3ba spots around hemogenic/EHT cells.
source: Interestingly, the number of hemogenic/EHT cells does not correlate with the absolute number of spots (Figure 4F, left panel, R=0.34), but rather it strongly correlates with the spatial densification of spots around hemogenic/EHT cells: the shorter the distance of the majority of spots are of hemogenic/EHT cells (Figure 4F, middle and right panel, representing 50% and 75% of spots, respectively), the higher the hemogenic/EHT cell count (R=–0.84 and R=–0.83, respectively).
evidence: This is based on correlation analysis of spatial RNAscope data.

claim: AECs expressing Pard3ba mRNAs are mostly in direct contact with cells committed to undergo EHT.
source: This shows that AECs expressing Pard3ba mRNAs are mostly in direct contact with cells committed to undergo EHT and suggests a signalling crosstalk occurring between them.
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial proximity of Pard3ba expression to hemogenic/EHT cells.

claim: Tri-junctional pools localized at antero-posterior poles of EHT cells enriched with eGFP-Jam3b molecules are significantly more dynamic for EHT pol+ cells in comparison to EHT pol- cells.
source: Altogether and unexpectedly regarding our initial scenario, these results indicate that tri-junctional pools localized at antero-posterior poles of EHT cells and enriched with eGFP-Jam3b molecules are significantly more dynamic for EHT pol+ cells in comparison to EHT pol- cells.
evidence: This is based on FRAP measurements comparing the two cell types.

claim: The median value of early recovery slopes for EHT pol+ - EC versus EHT pol- - EC junctional interfaces is increased by 128%.
source: Although smaller, differences in recovery were also measured between EHT pol+ – EC and EHT pol- – EC junctional interfaces when focusing on the earliest time points (the first 30 s, Figure 6F), with the median value of early recovery slopes for the EHT pol+ - EC versus EHT pol- – EC junctional interfaces increased by 128% (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of FRAP data.

claim: ArhGEF11, ArhGEF12b, Tiam1b and Tiam2a are significantly reduced upon dt-runx1 expression at 48 hpf.
source: We found that, in comparison to controls, ArhGEF11, ArhGEF12b, Tiam1b and Tiam2a are significantly reduced upon dt-runx1 expression at 48 hpf, hence being positively controlled in the wild-type condition, when the emergence of EHT cells is peaking.
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data comparing control and dt-runx1 conditions.

claim: Interfering with ArhGEF11 exon 38 splicing leads to accumulation of hemogenic cells in the aortic floor.
source: For the morphants, we found approximately a double amount of hemogenic cells in the aortic floor in comparison to controls (altogether localized on the floor and on the lateral sides of the aorta, see Figure 7A, panels in (a) for 2D-cartographies to visualize cell shapes, with the accumulation of hemogenic cells delineated in yellow for one morphant on the right and panels in (a') for cell counts of endothelial, hemogenic and EHT cells either in the entire aorta in trunks [left] or, more precisely, the aortic floor and lateral aortic side and the roof[right]; see also Figure 7—figure supplement 5 for additional examples).
evidence: This is based on quantitative morphometric analysis of confocal imaging data.

claim: Interfering with ArhGEF11 exon 38 splicing leads to a significant reduction in the number of morphologically characterized EHT cells.
source: This is accompanied by a significant reduction in the number of morphologically characterized EHT cells (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of cell counts from imaging data.

claim: A significant increase in the aortic perimeter was found for ArhGEF11 morphants.
source: Consistently, a significant increase in the aortic perimeter was found, at least for the morphants (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is based on morphometric measurements from imaging data.

claim: Hemogenic cells in ArhGEF11 morphants are on average less elongated in comparison to control and to the CRISPR homozygous mutants.
source: Of notice also, hemogenic cells in morphants are on average less elongated in comparison to control and to the CRISPR homozygous mutants (as well as less dispersed according to this parameter, compare Figure 7A, panel (a''') with Figure 7B, panel (b'''), with visualization of the dispersion on right panels).
evidence: This is based on morphometric analysis of cell shape from imaging data.

claim: Interfering with ArhGEF11 exon 38 splicing leads to an increase in the number of hemogenic/EHT cells in the aortic floor.
source: We show that, in agreement with our morphometric analysis, an increase in the number of hemogenic/EHT cells in the aortic floor in morphants in comparison to control embryos (Figure 7—figure supplement 7D, with median values of 14.0 and 22.5 hemogenic/EHT cells for controls and morphants, respectively).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of CD41:eGFP expressing cells.

claim: Interfering with ArhGEF11 exon 38 splicing leads to a relative diminution in the number of newly generated HSPC precursors.
source: Additionally, we observe, despite the high variability in both controls and morphants, a relative diminution in the number of newly generated HSPC precursors (Figure 7—figure supplement 7E, with median values of 22.0 and 16.5 HSPCs for controls and morphants, respectively).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of CD41:eGFP expressing cells that are kdrl-negative.

claim: ArhGEF11 exerts important functions in the EHT process.
source: Altogether, the morphants and CRISPR mutant phenotypes show that the progression throughout EHT is significantly impaired supporting the idea that ArhGEF11 exerts important functions in the process.
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypes observed upon ArhGEF11 interference.

claim: In ArhGEF11 morphants, there is an increase in FRAP recovery parameters for eGFP-Jam3b pools at the tri-junctional HE-HE-EC interface in comparison to controls.
source: In the case of the MO treatment (in which case HE cells accumulate on the aortic floor, see the 2D cartography (Figure 8A)) we measured, in comparison to controls, an increase in FRAP recovery parameters for eGFP-Jam3b pools at the tri-junctional HE-HE-EC interface, with a prominent tendency for an increase in the recovery speed at early time points (Figure 8B, panel (b'''), values obtained from fluorescence intensity recoveries whose mean values are represented by curves in panel (b''); compare with maximum recovery amplitudes (b'), with values obtained from the plateaus of fluorescence recovery intensities whose mean values are represented in panel (b)).
evidence: This is based on FRAP measurements at specific junctional interfaces.

claim: In ArhGEF11 CRISPR C-terminal deletion mutants, there is a small tendency for an increase in the mobile pool at HE-EC-EC tri-junctions.
source: Results are different for the ArhGEF11CRISPR-Cterdel+/+ homozygous mutants for which we did not observe any obvious effect at HE-HE-EC tri-junctions (Figure 8C, with the panels (c - c''') mirroring the presentations of results obtained for morphants and internal controls in Figure 8B) but, rather, a small tendency for an increase in the mobile pool at HE-EC-EC tri-junctions (that has the particularity to concern 2 endothelial cells that contact the longitudinal membrane of one HE cell, see Figure 8A and D).
evidence: This is based on FRAP measurements at specific junctional interfaces.
